subject: Partner paper: billing flow, fee allocation & MSA/Order Form alignment
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <amercer@skylinecloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partner paper draft + billing flow questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning — we had a good sync with product and finance. Attached is our initial partner paper draft and the Order Form we expect to use for the Skyline marketplace listing (OrderForm_Skyline_2026-08-05.pdf). Two quick items we need your input on:

1) Fee pass-through language: Skyline's finance team would like a short clause that clarifies that Marketplace fees (platform surcharge and reseller fee) are collected by Skyline from end customers and then remitted to Redwood on a monthly basis. They want to make sure taxes and gross-up language are explicit.

2) Invoicing and reconciliation: We propose monthly aggregated usage reporting with settlement net-30. Can Redwood confirm this cadence and whether Redwood will accept Skyline invoices or whether Redwood will instead invoice Skyline for the platform amount?

I've CC'd our contracts mailbox for visibility. If Redwood has a standard addendum for cloud marketplace listings that calls out routing, billing, and tax responsibilities, please send — that will speed the redline process on our side.

Attachments: Skyline_Partner_Paper_v1.docx, OrderForm_Skyline_2026-08-05.pdf

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Partnerships, SkylineCloud
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <amercer@skylinecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Skyline Contracts <contracts@skylinecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper draft + billing flow questions

Hi Alex — thanks for sending the draft. We're aligned on moving quickly here; happy to close billing flow and pass-through language in the next few rounds of redlines. Quick responses to your two bullets:

1) Pass-through language: Redwood's preference is that marketplace operator (Skyline) invoices the end customer for the aggregate amount, retains any marketplace platform surcharge, and remits Redwood's portion (our standard list price less agreed discount) on a monthly settlement. We do require a clause that Skyline will provide line-item usage reports (customer, SKU, quantity, gross charge, taxes) to enable our reconciliation.

2) Invoicing cadence: Net-30 monthly settlement works for us. Redwood typically issues invoices to partners (Skyline) for amounts due to Redwood; however we are flexible if Skyline can provide a single net-settlement invoice that matches our ledger. The key is matched line-item detail for reconciliation.

Laura and Karthik — looping you both in to review contract language. Laura, I attached Redwood's MSA addendum template (MSA_Addendum_Template.docx) which contains our suggested marketplace billing clauses. Can you please: 1) review for redlineable language around tax gross-up and indemnities, and 2) propose a short fallback if reconciliations don't match (e.g., escrow holdback or dispute window)?

Alex — once we have Laura's redlines we can propose a single tracked doc and a 30-minute call to run through open items.

Thanks — Soojin

Soojin Lee
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Skyline Contracts <contracts@skylinecloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <amercer@skylinecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-08T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper draft + billing flow questions

Hi Soojin / Alex,

Thanks for the context. A couple of internal questions we flagged while reviewing the MSA addendum:

- Who is the "invoicing party" for Redwood-recognized revenue? In some marketplace flows the partner invoices the customer and then Redwood invoices the partner; in others Redwood invoices the customer directly through the marketplace. We need to lock this down for tax reporting.

- Tax & withholding: If Skyline is collecting and remitting certain taxes on customer invoices (we expect to do this in several EU jurisdictions), does Redwood accept that Skyline's remittance will reduce the amount due to Redwood or should Redwood calculate tax separately?

- Credits/chargebacks: Please confirm a proposed dispute window (we suggest 45 days from invoice date) and whether Redwood can hold disputed amounts in a short-term escrow pending reconciliation.

We'll start redlining once we get any suggested clause language from Redwood for the above.

Regards,
Skyline Contracts Team
contracts@skylinecloud.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Skyline Contracts <contracts@skylinecloud.com>, Alex Mercer <amercer@skylinecloud.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-08T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Partner paper draft + billing flow questions (redlines attached)

Folks — attached is a quick pass with suggested language (redlines_MSA_section5.docx). High-level suggestions below:

1) Invoicing party: We recommend contract language that states Skyline will invoice the end customer via the marketplace; Skyline will collect all gross customer charges (including customer-facing marketplace platform surcharges). Redwood will issue an invoice to Skyline for Redwood's portion of the gross charges as calculated per the Order Form and settlement report. This keeps tax reporting with the party that remitted taxes to authorities while preserving Redwood's right to audit reports.

2) Tax treatment: Proposed clause: "All taxes imposed on the sale to the end customer shall be identified and remitted by the invoicing party. Redwood's settlement obligation shall be calculated on the gross charges net of taxes that are required to be collected and remitted by the invoicing party. Any taxes withheld by law shall be treated as a grossing-up event as described in Section X." (See redlines for exact wording.)

3) Disputes & holdback: We propose a 45-day dispute window from invoice issuance. For materially disputed amounts (>5% of an invoice) Redwood may request a short-term holdback pending reconciliation; requested holdbacks should be reconciled within 60 days.

Practical note: Karthik / Soojin, if Skyline prefers to issue a single consolidated invoice that already nets Redwood's portion (i.e., Skyline remits Redwood's share before invoicing Redwood), that is acceptable provided Skyline supplies the raw line-item usage export in the format specified in Appendix A of the attached redlines. We also included sample clause text for audit rights and data retention (we prefer 24 months retention of line-item usage).

Next steps I recommend: 1) Alex / Skyline to confirm whether Skyline will be the primary invoicing party; 2) if yes, Sky to accept the line-item report format or propose mapping; 3) mutual action plan + DocuSign routing once we have agreement on tax/gross-up language.

Attachments: redlines_MSA_section5.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-09T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper draft + billing flow questions (next steps)

Alex / Contracts team — thanks for the quick turnaround and Laura for the clear redlines. Summary and proposed next steps below: 

Summary:
- Agreed model: Skyline to invoice end customers; Skyline will collect marketplace surcharges and remit Redwood's portion monthly.
- Redwood will invoice Skyline for Redwood's portion per Order Form if Skyline cannot provide a matching consolidated settlement invoice.
- Tax/gross-up: Use Laura's proposed clause; Skyline to confirm whether taxes withheld at source will be grossed up or netted per jurisdiction.
- Disputes: 45-day dispute window; holdback for material disputes (>5%), reconciliation within 60 days.

Action items:
1) Alex / Skyline to confirm invoicing party (one-line reply) and whether Skyline accepts the Appendix A line-item format (due EOD 2026-08-10).
2) Laura to produce a tracked doc merging Redwood MSA addendum with Skyline partner paper (Laura to own).
3) Karthik / Soojin to coordinate with finance/ops on mapping (billing SKU mapping, settlement file fields) — propose 30-minute technical handoff on 2026-08-12 10:00am PT.
4) Once tracked doc is mutually agreed, route for signature via DocuSign (we'll use the link in related_links).

Alex — can you confirm item (1) above? If Skyline confirms they will be the invoicing party and can deliver the line-item export, we can prepare the tracked doc and aim to sign by the end of next week.

Thanks all — looks straightforward to close with the proposed model.

Best,
Soojin
